messages:
Priya: koala-prod reporting high tail latency + 429s from dedicated pool rpool-koala-3 starting ~2026-02-12T10:12Z. P95 jumped ~600ms -> 2.4s, customers seeing early aborts and billing noise. Linking grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/koala/overview?panelId=5 :eyes:
Marco: can you paste node/pod ids and the MIG profile? first suspicion is MIG sibling SM/DRAM thrash after an autoscale. check `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `nvtop` around the spike window.
Sam: quick snapshot from 10:11-10:15 from the node (redacted):
```
# node: rnode-az3-014
GPU0  util: 98%  mem: 14656MiB  MIG profiles: 3g.20gb
GPU1  util: 12%  mem: 243MiB
SM  saturated on GPU0 for 20s, PCIe rx/tx jitter seen
```

infra-oncall: we saw an autoscaler event at 10:10:52 that removed two fractional pods and repacked slices on that host. packing change coincides with the spike. autoscaler logs: `scaleDown: candidate=rpool-koala-3 count=2 reason=low_util` then immediate upscale at 10:12:08.
Jen: please capture the exact `mig-describe` output and the host-level nvlink/fabric metrics. fractional packing + repack during burst = classic co-residency shock. Also need the tenant request pattern (short-seq vs long-seq).
Priya: tenant pattern: mostly short seq chat inference, high qps bursts. attached simplified request histogram (short sequences dominate).
Marco: repro suggestion: run a synthetic workload that mimics Koala's pattern on a sibling slice while sampling `nvml` SM/warp stalls and L2 hit rates. Example stress command we use for repro:
```
# run on test host (isolated)
python infra/tools/loadgen.py --model gpt-small --qps 120 --seq 32 --duration 10m --kv_warmup 0.6
```

Sam: ran quick isolated load on sibling slice; saw SM saturation and a KV cache miss spike when the other slice warmed its KV (timing aligns). Logs excerpt: `kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.38 -> 0.61` and `sm_activity: 0.72 -> 0.98`.
infra-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) pin Koala to a reserved host (no fractional packing) 2) set autoscaler cooldown to 5m to avoid quick repack churn 3) bump pool capacity by 1 slice while we investigate. Which do you want while we triage?
Priya: start with bump + cooldown. Koala is OK with a short capacity bump; want to avoid customer impact. Please create a support case ID and note potential billing blip.
support-bot: created case #C-2026-0927-koala-noise, escalated to eng-runtime and infra-oncall.
Jen: root cause hypothesis: repack during burst caused a high-occupancy MIG slice to be colocated with a warm-up-heavy neighbor; KV warmup IO & SM saturation produced transient tail latencies and auth 429s when internal token throttles hit. Plan: repro in staging with exact MIG profile, capture nvml counters, then validate two mitigations: conservative packing (no fractional) and autoscaler cooldown. I'll own the runtime test.
Marco: parity checklist for repro: 1) exact MIG profile 2) sequence distribution 3) burst QPS shaping 4) observe KV cache warmup timeline 5) capture p95/p99 and nvml counters.
Sam: I'll schedule a staging window and run the load tomorrow 09:30 UTC, will post results here.
Priya: thank you — please add any billing notes to case. Keep me posted, i'll update the customer we have a mitigation in flight :thumbsup:
Jen: once we repro i'll test strict isolation + fractional packing disabled and report delta. If both mitigations help, recommend policy: small pools with short-seq bursty tenants should default to no-fractional-packing and a 3-5m autoscaler cooldown.
infra-oncall: implemented temporary capacity bump + set autoscaler.cooldown=300s for rpool-koala-3. Monitoring for next 30m.
Sam: first staging run scheduled and documented in the case.
Priya: ack, will wait for run results.
